topic: Probabilistic Early Refresh Halts Redis Stampedes
postText:
Every night shift, when clinical duty rosters rotated, identical cache keys expired at the exact same second.
Our Postgres connection pool spiked to 100% capacity in milliseconds, freezing emergency triage read paths.

We relied on classic Cache-Aside:
Cache miss -> Query DB -> Set Redis key with static 10-minute TTL.

The flaw? When hundreds of ward tablets poll duty rosters simultaneously at 07:00, hard TTL expiry triggers a brutal cache stampede. Every app replica hits a cache miss simultaneously and hammers the primary database with identical heavy JOIN queries.

Distributed mutex locks (SETNX) mitigate this, but lock contention at peak throughput spikes p99 tail latency and burns application worker threads.

Our production fix: Probabilistic Early Expiration (the XFetch algorithm).
Instead of waiting for TTL to hit zero, incoming reads evaluate DB recompute latency against remaining key lifetime with an exponential random variable:
-(delta * beta * ln(random())) > remaining_ttl

When condition triggers, that single client initiates a background cache recompute while immediately returning current data. No thread blockage, no database pileup, and cache remains continuously warm.

How do you handle hot key stampedes in your production clusters—distributed mutex, XFetch probabilistic refresh, or scheduled cron warming?
